chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a mouse that falls into the well, and it is not known about until after wudu (ablution) has been performed from it. Should the salat (prayer) be repeated? He said: No.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which the water was taken
key_terms.لَا: a negation indicating that repetition is not required

ai.seo_question: If a mouse fell into a well and I only found out after performing wudu (ablution), must I repeat my salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a mouse falling into a well when its presence was only discovered after wudu (ablution) had already been performed from that water. The Imam عليه السلام ruled that the salat (prayer) does not have to be repeated, indicating validity in this case despite later discovery.
